questions.question: Which structures make up the central nervous system?
choices: Brain and spinal cord
Heart and blood vessels
All muscles and tendons
Thyroid and adrenal glands

questions.question: What is a neuron?
choices: A gland specialized for releasing hormones into blood
A cell specialized for storing mineral in bone
A cell specialized for transmitting information
A protein specialized for speeding chemical reactions

questions.question: What is a synapse?
choices: A whole endocrine gland
A communication junction between a neuron and another cell
A kidney filtering unit
A type of blood vessel

questions.question: What is a neurotransmitter?
choices: A hormone transported only through the bloodstream
A receptor located in an endocrine cell membrane
A structural protein supporting the neuron
A chemical signal used at many synapses

questions.question: What is a hormone?
choices: An impulse traveling along a motor neuron's membrane
A receptor that binds a signal outside a cell
A protein forming a synaptic communication junction
A chemical messenger released by endocrine cells

questions.question: What is a receptor in cell signaling?
choices: A messenger released into the bloodstream
A molecule that binds a particular signal
An organ that coordinates several body systems
A pathway that carries nerve impulses

questions.question: Which gland produces insulin?
choices: Thyroid
Pineal gland
Pancreas
Adrenal cortex

questions.question: Why do hormones affect some cells more directly than others?
choices: Target cells have suitable receptors
Every cell responds equally to any circulating hormone
A hormone affects only the closest cell regardless of receptors
Target cells must produce the hormone themselves

questions.question: How do nervous and endocrine signaling commonly differ?
choices: Hormonal signals always arrive faster than nerve impulses
Nerve signals are often rapid; hormonal effects can be more widespread
Nerve signals travel mainly through the bloodstream
Hormones act only on the cells that release them

questions.question: Why can a reflex response occur before conscious awareness of a stimulus?
choices: Every reflex requires conscious interpretation first
Motor neurons send the initial signal from skin to the brain
Reflexes use hormones instead of coordinating nerve circuits
Some responses are coordinated through circuits such as those in the spinal cord

questions.question: What role do sensory neurons commonly serve?
choices: Carry information from receptors toward the central nervous system
Carry only motor commands to muscles
Release all hormones into blood
Form every synapse's receiving muscle

questions.question: What role do motor neurons commonly serve?
choices: Detect every blood chemical directly
Filter waste from blood
Carry commands to effectors such as muscles
Carry only information from skin toward the brain

questions.question: How does myelin help many axons?
choices: It slows conduction so each signal remains longer
It produces the hormones carried by the neuron
It supports faster impulse conduction
It acts as the receptor for every neurotransmitter

questions.question: How does insulin usually affect elevated blood glucose?
choices: It promotes processes that lower blood glucose
It stimulates processes that increase blood glucose
It prevents cells from storing glucose
It acts only on blood pressure, without glucose effects

questions.question: Why is hormonal negative feedback useful?
choices: It makes responses grow after the original change has ended
It prevents the regulated variable from being detected
It maintains hormone release regardless of target conditions
It limits responses as regulated conditions approach their target range

questions.question: A signal is present in blood but a cell lacks its receptor. What is expected in the basic model?
choices: The cell has the same direct response as a target cell
The cell does not show that receptor-dependent response
The signal automatically supplies the missing receptor
The cell responds by releasing every available hormone

questions.question: A hand withdraws rapidly from an unpleasant stimulus. Which sequence best describes a simple reflex arc?
choices: Receptor → sensory neuron → coordinating circuit → motor neuron → muscle
Receptor → motor neuron → coordinating circuit → sensory neuron → muscle
Muscle → sensory neuron → gland → receptor → brain
Receptor → bloodstream → digestive organ → bone → muscle

questions.question: A model shows a gland releasing a messenger into blood to affect distant target cells. Which system is emphasized?
choices: Skeletal
Endocrine
Digestive mechanical processing
Integumentary barrier formation

questions.question: Nerve signals to a muscle increase while other conditions remain suitable. Which effect is plausible?
choices: Muscle activity becomes independent of all motor signals
The muscle produces hormones instead of responding to neurons
The signal is interpreted only by nearby bones
A change in muscle activation

questions.question: A control loop reduces hormone release after the regulated variable returns toward normal. Which pattern is illustrated?
choices: Positive feedback
Feedforward control without feedback
Negative feedback
An unregulated continuous response
